rulesRejectedFramesNote:
THE THREE FRAMES THE COLOUR TEST REJECTS ARE KEPT, AND THE RULE THAT REJECTS THEM IS LEFT ALONE. After the restructure `pnpm check-evidence` fails exactly these three and nothing else. Each was put through the owner's test (2026-09-25): is this asset referenced by a README, by `docs/`, or by in-app code or tests, or is it evidence for a PR or a code change only? ALL THREE ARE REFERENCED, so all three stay. RESULT PER FRAME, with the search that produced it - the search ran over every tracked text file (binaries excluded by extension), matching each frame's repository-relative path, its `docs/evidence`-relative path, its bare filename and its stem: (1) `canvas-file-freshness/html-before/localOperatorDark.webp` - mode `#FFFFFF` over 39.25% of the frame, DELTA-E00 72.52 from the nearest `localOperatorDark` ground; opened and looked at, it is the app (dark chrome, document tabs, the mtime line, the viewer's `Edit` toggle) with the viewer's own embedded HTML document filling the right-hand pane in white, so the mode is the DOCUMENT's colour and the frame is not a blank capture. Referenced by `docs/evidence/canvas-file-freshness/README.md` (its table row at `README.md:72`, which cites design round 2's D8) and by no other file. (2) `canvas-file-freshness/html-after/localOperatorDark.webp` - mode `#FFFFFF` over 39.24%; its row at `README.md:82` carries code review round 1's M1 - same finding, same single reference. (3) `run-panel-reveal/press-800x600-after-fix/localOperatorLight.webp` - mode `#1E1A15`, a DARK frame filed under the light palette: DELTA-E00 81.86 from the nearest `localOperatorLight` ground and 2.19 from the nearest `localOperatorDark` ground (`sunken`, `#1d1b19`; its next-nearest grounds are 2.31, 4.11 and 6.77). It is not a byte copy of its sibling (66162 B against 62996 B, different sha256), so it is a distinct capture whose light half either never applied the palette or was committed under the wrong name; the `.json` beside it is the light run's own reading. Referenced by `docs/evidence/run-panel-reveal/README.md` (its frame-pairing block and the readings table's `800x600 / expanded / after-fix / light` row) and by no other file. PROPOSED AND NOT APPLIED - the minimal rule change the two canvas frames need: the gate asks whether the MODE is within DELTA-E00 25 of the ground of the palette the filename names, and a frame whose subject is an embedded document cannot satisfy that while still being a picture of the app. Accept a frame when the mode is within the ceiling OR when a MAJORITY of its pixels are within the ceiling of the named theme's grounds. Measured on this tree with the gate's own palette source and colour maths: the two canvas frames sit at 59.39% of pixels within the ceiling of `localOperatorDark`, three frames that pass today sit at 95.98% (`run-panel-reveal/press-800x600-after-fix/localOperatorDark.webp`), 98.97% (`canvas-file-freshness/after/localOperatorDark.webp`) and 99.32% (`browser-webauthn/chooser-answered/localOperatorDark.webp`), and the third frame above sits at 2.00% of pixels within the ceiling of the palette its name carries - so the proposal would keep failing exactly the case the check exists for and would not rescue a misnamed capture. THE RULE IS UNCHANGED IN THIS PASS: with it as written, one of the three (the misnamed light frame) cannot pass under any change that does not also stop the gate seeing a wrong-theme capture, and the honest repairs for it are a re-capture of that light half (`scripts/run-panel-reveal-proof.mjs --theme=localOperatorLight` at 800x600) or its removal, neither of which this pass was asked to decide.

ADDENDUM, 2026-09-30 (the evidence-record clearing pass; no re-capture of these two frames, no rule change): the two canvas-file-freshness frames were re-verified against `origin/main` = `dad1778e148dd5a8d86db463f38c1d4a4cbc9087`, and nothing about them has moved - `html-before` and `html-after` are the SAME blobs they have been since `c4f1615864` (`docs(evidence): re-take the frames for the row's floor, and re-stamp after the fold`, 2026-09-18), byte-identical to HEAD. That is every number this note quotes for them, unchanged - the byte identity is why. THEY REMAIN THE SWEEP'S SCOPED, DOCUMENTED PAINT EXCEPTIONS, and the majority-criterion rule revision above stays PROPOSED AND NOT APPLIED: a gate policy change is out of this pass's scope, which fixes records rather than rules. Item (3) is likewise resolved by this pass: `run-panel-reveal/press-800x600-after-fix/localOperatorLight.webp` was re-shot with the set's own rig (`b6e19627a8`, on `dad1778e14`, 2026-09-30) and now reads as the palette it is named for - mode `#F2EDE3`, DELTA-E00 0.00 from the nearest `localOperatorLight` ground - with its JSON replaced by the run's own; the sweep no longer reports it.

RESOLVED BY RE-SHOOT, 2026-10-03 (`bd4c95f77`, the #775 fold): items (1) and (2) are closed without a rule change or an exception. `canvas-file-freshness/html-{before,after}/localOperatorDark.webp` were re-taken with the set's own scene in its one whole-set pass; the fresh frames' mode colour is the `localOperatorDark` ground itself, `#22201C`, covering 34.46% of the frame (against the previous generation's `#FFFFFF` at 39.25% and 39.24%), and the gate's own predicates (`frameHistogram` + `assertFramePaints`) return clean on both. imageExpandPass.notCovered: A real-engine pointer press aimed at a POINT outside the picture. A coordinate-capable harness closes it - QA's place, named in the set's README rather than implied away.

partialCapture.publishInstructionSetPass:
THIS FOLD'S OWN PASS, AND THE THREE THINGS THE RE-TAKE FOUND. Run at `8b6dacf2d` against a private Storybook on this worktree, as two narrowed runs - `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://localhost:6041 --only=agents-publish-dialog` (132 frames) and `--only=agents-pull-outcomes` (60) - on a worktree whose `.env` points `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` at a dead port, so no frame could quote the live backend and `--allow-backend` was not needed. All 192 frames were RE-TAKEN rather than re-stamped: the sixty pull frames and ten of the eleven dialog directories came back byte-identical to the frames this branch had already committed, and the rest did not.

(1) THE STORE LEAKED BETWEEN STORIES - AND ONLY UNDER THE SANCTIONED NARROWING. `NameTakenByYou`'s play republishes, the stub accepts, and the app's accepted-publication path writes the listing into `published-listings-store`, which is `persist`ed to localStorage; the component that was supposed to contain it cleared on UNMOUNT, and the capture replaces the whole document per story, so React never unmounts what it has just photographed. Five frames - `name-claim-in-flight`, `reserved-builtin`, `reserved-builtin-refusal`, `moderation-rejected`, `moderation-unavailable` - therefore photographed the dialog's UPDATE state (`Update the Agent hub listing for "..."`, the update affordance, and no availability line) instead of the refusal each is named for. Taken one story per run, with a fresh browser profile each time, all five were right; taken as the family the table declares, five were wrong. That is the property that was lost, and this file has no field that could record it. Fixed in `0b7aece10` by resetting the store at module scope, once per story document and before the first render.

(2) ONE WAIT TEXT WAS SHARED WITH THE ALERT. `ReservedBuiltin`'s play waited for `is the name of a built-in agent`, and that sentence is in the pre-validation ALERT as well as in the courtesy line the availability check writes - while the alert paints a 400 ms debounce and a fetch earlier. The wait returned on the alert and the shutter raced the answer: one pass photographed both lines in eleven themes and only the alert in `localOperatorDark`, and the next pass moved the missing theme to `dracula` and `monokai`. Fixed in `66983f73d`, by waiting on `which the hub reserves`, which the alert does not contain.

(3) A STATE THAT APPEARED COULD STILL LEAVE BEFORE THE SHUTTER. `settleOn` released the shutter the moment its text painted, which is too early for an answer-produced state whose inputs are live - the debounced name field, an enable flag: two consecutive family passes on the same commit disagreed about `default/localOperatorDark` (no courtesy line against the line), and both plays had already seen the text. Fixed in `8b6dacf2d`: the wait now requires the text to HOLD for a beat (800 ms, longer than the debounce it has to outlast) with the shutter held throughout, and fails loudly rather than releasing onto a state on its way out. Measured afterwards on two consecutive family passes: 132 frames, no difference outside lossy-WebP encoder noise - `magick compare -fuzz 5%` reports zero on the two frames that differ at all.

THAT MEASUREMENT WAS TOO COARSE, AND ROUND 1'S QA FALSIFIED IT. `published/` was not byte-stable: 1-2 of its twelve themes per pass flipped between exactly two hashes, with `cwebp` returning identical bytes for the same PNG twice, so it was a render difference rather than encoder noise. A `-fuzz 5%` comparison scores it as zero because the delta is sub-perceptual - max 13/255, 89% of the differing pixels within 1-2 levels, and the whole bounding box (`204x72+604+520`) sits on the footer's action row. Re-measured at zero fuzz on two twelve-theme passes: the difference is a `:focus-visible` ring drawn around an action in one variant and absent in the other. Its cause, and the fix, are recorded in the same object under the key below, `publishInstructionSetRemediationRoundOne`.

TWO STALE FRAMES WERE CORRECTED, and they are why a re-stamp could not stand: `default/localOperatorDark` and `reserved-builtin/localOperatorDark` shipped WITHOUT the courtesy line under the name field while their eleven sibling themes carried it. The set was internally inconsistent about the one line two of these stories exist to photograph.

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT CLAIM: that the hub answers any of these shapes. The live hub does not implement the contract's availability route - `https://api.radienthq.com/v1/agent-name-availability` answers 404 at this head, measured, not assumed - and every frame here is a stub's answer in the shape the contract names.
partialCapture.publishInstructionSetRemediationRoundOne:
ROUND 1'S REMEDIATION, ON THE SAME TREE, RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN RE-STAMPED: `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://localhost:6041 --only=agents-publish-dialog` (132 frames) and `--only=agents-pull-outcomes` (60), twice each, on a worktree whose `.env` points `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` at a dead port, so no frame can quote a live backend and `--allow-backend` is neither needed nor passed. All 192 frames are re-taken. The frames are a function of this tree: every read the rig needs is answered by the story's own stubbed transport, including the connectivity probe's `/health`, which is what lets the pre-flight frame show the instruction-body rule it claims.

THE FLAKE THE ROUND FOUND, AND WHY IT WAS REAL. `published/` photographed two states: the footer's action row with a `:focus-visible` ring on the primary action, and the same row without it. Both are this app's own rendering - `cwebp -q 78` on the same PNG twice returns identical bytes, and `capture-evidence.mjs` writes through Chromium's own encoder - so an encoder could not alternate between exactly two states per theme. THE CAUSE IS FOCUS PLACEMENT PLUS THE ENGINE'S MODALITY HEURISTIC, not the encoder and not the pixels: Radix moves focus onto the dialog container as the panel opens, and this dialog's submit button LEAVES THE DOM when an outcome replaces the form, so every refusal and receipt state photographed whatever Blink's focus fixup chose next - sometimes the container, sometimes the new action row. Focusing the primary action explicitly (a layout effect, which beats the fixup) pins WHERE focus goes but NOT whether the ring is drawn: `:focus-visible` for a programmatically focused element is decided from the engine's last-interaction modality, which an app cannot set and a synthetic click does not set deterministically. Measured with the focus pinned: the same 1-2 themes per pass still flipped.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD. The ring is removed where it is noise rather than placed where it is undecidable. A result state focuses its own result region - a plain container, not a control, carrying `outline-none`, which `styles/index.css` names as the sanctioned case for "focus is moved there programmatically and a ring would be noise" - and this dialog's panel container is silenced the same way through `BaseDialog`'s `dialogProps`, scoped to this dialog rather than changed in the primitive, because five other dialogs' frames are not re-taken here and a shared visual change would silently invalidate them. Nothing in either family can ring except a real control reached by Tab.

MEASURED AFTERWARDS, at zero fuzz rather than at `-fuzz 5%`: two consecutive passes of each family, 192 frames each, byte-identical - zero differing frames. Five consecutive twelve-theme passes of `published`, and three of `name-taken`, were byte-identical too, which is the check that isolates the story the flake lived in. The pre-submit and refusal states that carried the same class of ring on the container are re-taken in this set.

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT CLAIM: that a ring is never the right answer here, or that the actions are reachable without a Tab press. It claims that these frames are a function of the tree, that the sink is where focus goes in every pass, and that the actions keep their own rings and stay one Tab press away.

WHAT UNBLOCKED IT, since the previous entry said the healthy re-capture was deferred as impossible: the harness seeded the provoking user turn AFTER `/rig-arm`, i.e. after `watching_surfaces()` went non-empty and therefore after the app had already been answered its history request. The durable row never reached the transcript, CanonicalTranscript collapsed to h-0 as designed, and the driver failed with `no fieldset` - which read as 'the driver cannot aim' but was a fixture armed one page-load too late. The turn is now appended before the SERVER ANNOUNCES ITSELF, so the history request sees it and the gate follows it, which is how the app always reaches this state. That is a harness fix, not a product change; QA round 2's Q1 is closed by running the committed rig rather than by re-labelling the gap.
Captured in localOperatorDark only: this is a wire-and-interaction proof, not a palette proof. The twelve-theme question is answered by chat-ask-options/, which the sweep takes across every palette.

WHAT THE `lost-report-*` PAIR IS FOR, and why it is a PAIR. The defect is an ORDERING, not a rendering, and it cannot be photographed out of a lucky run: the answer's response and the owner's state push have no ordering between them, and the ordinary run above shows how small the margin is, and NO MILLISECOND FIGURE IS QUOTED HERE ANY MORE (agent review round 2, MINOR-2): it is a fresh sample on every sweep - across this branch's sweeps the delivery has led the clearing by a millisecond and trailed it by a quarter of a second, and the `lost-report-*` pair's own hold has read 2638/2508ms and 2524/2511ms - so a quoted number is wrong the moment the set is re-taken, which is exactly how round 1's fix went stale. The numbers are the records' own: `answeredAt`, `deliveredAt`, `clearedAt` and `clearedAfterPressMs` in each `click-result.json`, and they are the ones to read. THE DOM FIGURE IS BOUNDED AND THE RECORD'S IS NOT: `clearedAt` is one sample of the driver's 250ms resolution poll, so `clearedAfterPressMs` is quantized to +/-250ms and is not a millisecond instrument, while `answeredAt`/`deliveredAt` are epoch milliseconds stamped in the rig's own process. `serve-gate.py --answer-delay-ms 2500` forces the losing order honestly - the request is delivered and the route runs untouched, the owner resolving the gate and pushing state at its normal moment, and only the DELIVERY of the response it already produced is held - so both runs answer 200, both record the owner taking the pressed label, and both record `"ordering": {"verdict": "the card cleared before the response was delivered"}`. lost-report-before/after-click/localOperatorDark.webp AND lost-report-after/after-click/localOperatorDark.webp ARE THE SAME RUN ON TWO TREES, and they are the whole claim: the first carries `That question was already answered somewhere else, so your answer was not sent.` under the composer of the build at `60c1dc615`, the base this branch folded onto while the owner has the answer, the second carries nothing at all on this branch's build. Each run's record says which it was without a reader having to trust the frame: `click-result.json`'s `report` block carries `settledSentence` and the `[role="alert"]` text, and the run was told what to expect (`CLICK_PROOF_EXPECT=settled` for the before build, `silent` for the after one) - a run whose composer disagrees writes `click-result.diagnostic.json` and leaves the committed record and frames untouched, so neither half of the pair can be overwritten by a run of the other.

THE 409 ARM IS NOT MERELY REASONED ABOUT HERE. `harness/probe-answer-exclusivity.py` drives the shipped answer route with no browser at all - two concurrent answers with different labels on one real gate, plus a stale third - and reports each status beside `owner-answer.json`, the owner's own return value. Six rounds: exactly one 2xx per gate, that request's label is the one the owner kept, and both losers are refused with a bare 409. That is the measurement behind `answerWasSettledElsewhere` keying the settled-elsewhere sentence on `status === 409 && code === undefined`, and behind the app no longer watching its own card to decide whether it won.

WHY THE FRAMES CARRY A RE-TAKE, stated here because the manifest's own `head` field is the citation a reader follows: main's window between this branch's cut (`305efc363`) and its fold (`60c1dc615`) moved `src/` (eleven files, including `message-input.tsx` and the composer's own `slash-*` modules), so the four fixed-build frames were re-taken on the folded tree rather than carried - a frame claimed as this tree's has to show this tree's composer. `head` therefore names the FOLD commit `faeabf8fa`, which is an ancestor of the head these frames ship in, and the before pair was taken with this branch's two files checked out of the working tree from that same base (`git checkout 60c1dc615 -- src/renderer/src/features/chat/ask-answer.ts src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-page.tsx`, NOT a `git stash`: the stash is machine-wide in this repository's shared `.git`, so an index-based pop is a lottery across the concurrent worktrees).

WHAT THE FIVE REFUSAL ARMS ARE FOR, since eight of the fourteen frames are new and three of them photograph states no earlier pass could reach. The answer route refuses with a BARE `409` in three different situations and only one of them is a settlement, so the app decides the sentence from LIVE facts rather than from the status; refused-card/ is a bare `409` written on a card that is still painted, refused-composer/ is the settled arm (another front end won, no gate pending), and unknown-composer/ is a request the app gave up on with the card already gone. unknown-card/ is the fifth and the one round 2 asked for (UX round 2, U7; QA round 2, Q1): the request is held past the app's own control deadline while the gate stays PENDING, so the outcome is unknowable and the card is still up - the state a plain press reaches, where the app used to print 'Your answer was not sent' and deny it in the next clause. THE REGISTER IS THE OUTCOME'S, NOT THE SURFACE'S: `answerReport` now chooses the sentence from the outcome class and only then the destination, so the card and the composer carry the same string for the same event (which is also what stopped a rollover refusal reading the backend's raw `detail` on the card and an authored sentence in the composer - UX round 2, U8). The card arm's options stay DISABLED in that frame (`after.disabled: [true, true, true]`), so the control cannot repeat an answer whose fate is unknown (UX round 2, U9). TWO OF THIS BRANCH'S SENTENCES HAVE NO FRAME and round 3 must not assume otherwise (design round 2, D7): the rollover sentence needs a moved owner epoch and the composer's moved-on sentence needs an ask that has advanced, and the shipped harness arms one question against one runtime, so neither state is reachable here. Both are asserted at the unit level instead, and the README's 'What is not framed here' says so.

supplementary.why: THE DRAWER STUCK OPEN OVER A CONVERSATION WITH NO ASKS, AND THIS DESKTOP SURFACE WAS THE LAST ONE STILL CARRYING THE TRAP (operator report, 2026-10-06). Read across the fleet: the TUI collapses its ask bar on a session swap and at a zero-row queue, and `_abandon_ask_surface`'s docstring names THIS class of defect as already fixed there ('the app stayed in ask mode with nothing mounted'); the phone's `AskDock` renders only when rows exist and its sheet is keyed by session and always draws chrome with its own empty/loading/error states; both read the capability as the presence of `asks` OR `asks_open`. The drawer instead declined to render at all when `sessionAsks(...)` was null, which was CORRECT until the runtime's wire fix made absence ambiguous - a live-but-empty queue is now published as `asks` ABSENT with `asks_open: 0` - and because the slot is claimed by the MOUNT (the open flag is the store's and `SessionPanel` is keyed by conversation) a component that renders `null` does not release it. WHAT THE FRAMES CARRY, as numbers: the before run reads `slotPresent: true` with `slotBox { x: 820, y: 0, w: 560, h: 900 }` and an empty `slotText` for six seconds of sampling and through both Escape arms, while the same path on the fixed tree reads `slotPresent: false` with every surface counter at zero. `live-before-switch-void` is that defect and `live-after-switch` is the same path fixed; the four `story-*` states are the ones no switch reaches on demand - the published-empty queue that now draws the panel's own empty sentence, an unresolved frame that must close nothing and trap nothing, a runtime that publishes no queued engine at all, and the wire bound's rowless frame whose list is gone while its tally stands - and they are the shipped stories `Chat/Asks/Queued asks -> Empty wire frame / Unread frame / Unsupported backend / Clipped rows frame`, so each frame can be opened by hand at the URL the rig used. WHAT ROUND 1'S REMEDIATION MOVED, in the same set: `story-unsupported/` is no longer byte-identical to `story-unread/` (a resolved frame that publishes no engine now states `Asks unavailable` instead of wearing a read that can never finish), the unread bar carries no clause at all (the body names that fact once), `story-clipped-rows/` is the rowless frame with a live tally that must keep its slot and state its count, and `live-after-new-chat-draft/` is the draft route a session-scoped drawer no longer follows onto. `live-run-after.json` carries its own deltas against `live-run-before.json`: the slot is still released, and conversation B - a live-but-empty queue - is now OFFERED its door (`headerTrigger: 1`, was 0), which is the capability read aligned to the wire contract (R3/Q1). WHAT ROUND 2 MOVED, and it is copy plus none of the live frames: `story-clipped-rows/`'s body drops its restatement of the bar's count and the wire's word for the payload (`The details for these asks could not be loaded.`; design round 2 D2-1 = UX round 2 U2-2), and `story-unsupported/`'s body says `doesn't support` rather than the wire's `publish` (UX round 2 U2-3). The round's MAJOR was a FOCUS-LANDING defect with no pixel of its own - a pane with no rows landed its entry focus on a `<div>` that cannot take it, so Escape was inert there - which is why no frame moves for it; the assertion that pins it is in `scripts/ask-draft-swap.test.mjs` (a door-opened pane with no rows lands focus inside the surface, where Escape closes). NOT CLAIMED HERE: no fleet-scope frame (opening the fleet trigger over an empty fleet needs every conversation empty, which this rig's session A - the session the ask lives on - is not), no Electron window (the renderer, the answer path and `/__desktop` are the shipping ones, the IPC/preload channel and a packaged window are not), and no pre-fix re-shoot from this harness (the before frames came from the session that reproduced the bug on the unfixed tree and are committed because the PAIR is the claim).

D1: the capability-withdrawn path had stopped rendering main's row box. The cause is main's `ce5fd9578` (`<button w-full>` -> `<div class="flex h-8 gap-1"><button min-w-0 grow>`), which this branch's fold kept in the ENABLED path while the withdrawn path went on returning a bare button - correct against this branch's base, wrong against main. The fix is one named constant (`rowBoxStyle`) rendered by BOTH paths, so the two cannot drift apart again, plus the test that asserts the identity rather than the spelling (`scripts/chat-sidebar-pins.test.mjs`); the scene grew the box's own check and the width check in response (`the conversation button FILLS the box around it`), because a shape-only check is what passed while the row was wrong. remediationRecord.qaRoundNineSceneInstrument: QA ROUND 9 ON THE ROUND-8 INSTRUMENT, and the finding of the round that was MAJOR. Q9-1: the focus-reveal block added in design round 8 focused the LAST conversation row, which made the browser scroll the region (`scrollTop 1075` on a 40-conversation store), and the press below then aimed at `pins[0]`'s STORED box - 416px above the viewport, `elementFromPoint` answering null - so the write never reached the backend and four checks failed for a reason of the scene's own making. The fix: the caret row and the press row are both taken from the rows ALREADY inside the region's window (a hoisted `visibleUnpinnedRows` plus a new `whollyInside`, so a partially visible row cannot make the browser scroll as the caret lands), the caret is moved by a REAL CDP Tab from the row's own button, the pin that is read is the one the CARET holds rather than one at an index, and the region is read back and asserted unchanged. The press reads what a click at its point would ACT on (the U3 instrument) before pressing. A/B on one rig, one daemon and one 40-conversation store: pre-fix scene 21 passed / 4 failed; fixed scene 84 / 0; fixed scene with only the focus block removed 76 / 0. And because a scene change can move the pixels it photographs: the pre-fix and fixed scenes were both run against the same daemon and the same 4-conversation store, and 12 of the 13 frames are byte-identical, the thirteenth differing by 66 pixels in one `2x33` box at `1098,1531` - the composer's caret, the same box this file's `reproducibility` field records. AND THE CHECK DISCRIMINATES, by a named mutation rather than by argument: with the pin control's `group-focus-within:opacity-100` removed from `chat-sidebar.tsx` (a hover-only control) and the app rebuilt, the same scene on the same 40-conversation store reports 49 passed / 1 failed, and the failing reading is the focus check with EVERY opacity `0` while the caret is verifiably ON the pin (`{"onButton":true,"inRow":true}` then `{"onPin":true,"subject":"Pin “Sweep 035”"}`) - so what fails is the reveal and not the instrument, which is the property the round asked for. The source edit was reverted and the tree rebuilt before this commit.

The other kind of field is the COUNTS - `frames`, `surfaces`, `themes`, `partialCapture.refreshedFrames` and the leading paragraph of every `countsMean` cell - and they describe the tree the frames SHIP in. They no longer include a stored hash of `src/` or `scripts/`: the retired `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` pair was exactly that, and a stored hash goes false for every open branch the moment any sibling commit moves either tree (measured on 2026-10-03: 32 first-parent merges onto `origin/main` in 24 hours, 29 of them moving `src/` or `scripts/`), so it forced a mechanical re-derive per fold and could never prove any frame had been freshly shot - every recorded re-derive in this file's history says 're-stamped, not re-captured'. WHEN MAIN AND THIS BRANCH BOTH REWRITE THIS FILE, THE MERGE IS A PER-FIELD DECISION AND NOT "KEEP MAIN'S RECORD", and it is per FIELD rather than per entry for the same reason: a union taken at entry granularity silently replaces an authored field inside an entry both sides have, which is how this branch's `why` clauses on `supplementary[wake-live-app]` and `supplementary[browser-pane-live]` vanished on the ninth fold (round 8, R8-2). The five groups, numbered as the rig's copy of this rule numbers them so the two homes cannot drift: (1) `head`, `headNote` and the `partialCapture` fields that DESCRIBE a pass - `refreshedAt`, `refreshedAtHead`, `refreshedFromHead`, `addedAt`, `addedAtHead`, `addedFrames`, `note`, `passScopeNote` and every per-pass `*Note` - are THIS branch's, because main's values name main's pass and taking them sends a verifier to a tree that does not carry this branch's frames; (2) the fields that LIST what both sides touched - `supplementary`'s ENTRIES, and `refreshedStories`, `refreshedThemes`, `addedSurfaces` - are the UNION of the two sides' entries or values, because the merged tree carries both and either side's list alone would claim a pass that did not run in it; (3) INSIDE a `supplementary` entry that exists on both sides, this pass's AUTHORED keys - `why`, `capturedAt`, `capturedAtHead` and any note - are KEPT and only the listings are unioned, since an entry is a record this branch wrote rather than a listing; (4) `refreshedFrames` is RE-DERIVED against HEAD rather than added up, and `frames`, `surfaces`, `themes` and the LEADING paragraph of every `countsMean` cell are re-derived from the merged tree and taken from neither side - `countsMean` belongs here because it restates `frames`/`surfaces`, and its prose says what each field counts and where to read it rather than carrying a number of its own, and only its LEAD is derived (the paragraphs under it are history by construction). The retired `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` pair sat in this group and is now RETIRED rather than derived: a fold DROPS it from both sides instead of re-deriving it, and the fold tool prints `dropped srcTree - retired by this change` so the loss is a stated decision rather than a silence; (5) NO FIELD THAT SPELLS OUT WHAT A CITATION NAMES is carried from main's side under any name - main's manifest still has `refreshedAtHeadNote`, the spelling this branch deleted, and carrying main's keys this branch lacks re-introduces it. Group (5) is stated once, here: earlier passes restated it in two more places in this field, which is the duplication round 9's R9-1 filed, and deleting them rather than re-pointing them is the same treatment the counts and the `why` clauses got. THE GATE'S TWO HALVES, named so the blind spot is auditable rather than summarised: `check-evidence.mjs` asks whether a citation RESOLVES (`citationFailures`) and whether it is an ANCESTOR OF `HEAD` (`citationAncestryFailures` - named by symbol rather than by line, since a line number is one more thing a later pass has to keep true). Main's own commit satisfies both, which is why the round-6 defect was invisible to it - and neither half asks whether the tree a citation names carries the frames this record declares. TWO CORRECTIONS THIS RULE NEEDED ONCE IT WAS EXERCISED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED, both found by the ninth fold: `countsMean` was listed in BOTH the keep-this-branch's group and the re-derive group, and a resolver reading the first one carried a stale prose count past a fold that had moved `frames`; and main's citation notes came back through the "carry main's keys this branch lacks" step, which is why group (5) exists. AND EVERY MERGED JSON/CONFIG FILE - this one included - IS KEY-CHECKED BY A GATE the rig's fold block carries as its item 6: `node scripts/check-fold-keys.mjs` compares the merged key set against BOTH parents' (nested objects walked; an array element that carries a `path` is keyed by it - the identity this file's own `supplementary` entries are paired by, so a loss inside ONE entry is visible even while its siblings still carry the same key - and an element without one by the union of its keys) and reports every key that left EITHER side - except a RETIRED key, the `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` pair this file no longer carries, whose disappearance from either side is reported as the deliberate retirement it is (`dropped srcTree - retired by this change`) rather than as a loss. A branch-side vanish is otherwise a fault unless the fold's record states the deliberate carry - the fold onto `44249a6796` took main's copy as the base for its list union, main had lost `check-themes` at `53c5cfec6b` (#714), and the key vanished while that fold reported a clean union (agent review round 8, R11; restored by the remediation commit it asked for). A main-side vanish must be either group (5) here, the retired-key exception above, or a stated repair. The gate does not see FORM - a re-imposed list prefix is not a key change - so a green run is not the whole union rule.

The first commit holds `NOTARIZE` in one `env:` block at the job, where a step added there cannot lose it by omission, and deliberately not at the workflow, because this workflow's `exact-update` job exists to run on a fresh VM with no Apple credentials at all. THE FOLLOW-UP CLOSES THE GAPS THOSE ROUNDS FOUND. M-2: the three `APPLE_*` credentials are SECRETS and are bound on the three steps that notarise - the two macOS passes, whose app bundles `scripts/notarize.js` notarises from `afterSign`, and the disk-image step - because at job scope they sat in the environment of all fourteen steps of that job, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` postinstall scripts and marketplace actions included, where they buy nothing. WRITTEN BY THE PASS THAT PUT THE SERVER RELEASE NOTES ON THE OFFER CARD (`feat(update): show what changed in the server release the offer names`). The panel that offers a server update named two versions and a benefit sentence and nothing about the change itself, while the app's own update card has carried notes since it was written; this pass reads them from the server's own GitHub release (`src/main/server-release-notes.ts`), carries them on the offer and renders them above the panel's arm split.

WHAT IT MOVES: both trees. Under `src/` - `src/main/server-release-notes.ts` (new), `src/main/update-service.ts`, `src/renderer/src/shared/components/common/update-notification.tsx` and its story file. Plus twenty-four new frames, in two stories. `frames` 9122 and `surfaces` 929 are that arithmetic, re-derived in the two fields above rather than carried.

WHAT WAS CAPTURED, AND HOW: `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://127.0.0.1:6033 --only=backend-update-with --allow-backend --theme-settle-ms=90000` - a narrowed run, so the committed set is appended to rather than swept. `--allow-backend` because the operator's own server answers on 1111 on this host and the stories are mocked-IPC payloads that never call it; `--theme-settle-ms=90000` because the shipped 10 s budget is a loaded-host failure (the first two attempts died with `document carries theme "" after 10s`). TWO STORIES: `common-updatenotification--backend-update-with-release-notes` is the reported state (0.62.33 serving, 0.62.34 offered) with the note the lookup read; `common-updatenotification--backend-update-with-long-release-notes` is the same offer carrying a summary AT the producer's 400-character budget, shot at 900x572 - the app's own minimum window, where the card's cap is 540px. Its row declares 556 rather than 572 because this story file's content asks for sixteen more pixels than it is declared at (the rig paints `max(documentElement.scrollHeight, body.scrollHeight, declared)` and both stories of this file come out declared+16), so 572 would paint a 588px viewport and a cap of 556 - one mono line more generous than the state it claims. `scripts/server-release-notes.test.mjs` runs the summariser over BOTH real bodies and fails if either fixture string stops being what the rule produces.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE, AND THE CONTROL THAT SAYS SO. No frame outside the two new directories is re-taken, and the reason is testable rather than argued: every other server-offer fixture in `update-notification.stories.tsx` carries no `releaseNotes`, so the new block cannot render on one. The control was run anyway: `--only=backend-update-non-managed` was re-captured at this head, and its twelve frames were then REVERTED, because this host's rig is not byte-reproducible against the committed set - the re-capture came back visually identical (same panel, same copy, no paragraph) with a per-pixel delta of 3.8-5.4% of pixels at a max channel delta of 115-162, and one palette differing at every pixel by a level or two, which is a different Chrome build and WebP encoder than the pass that wrote the committed set rather than a repaint. projectsSearchIndexWiringNote: THE SEARCH-INDEX WIRING ITSELF, for a reader arriving at the diff. The Projects search now asks the backend's derived index (`GET /v1/desktop/projects/search`, `projects` capability version 2) when the backend advertises it, and keeps the client matcher as the compatibility path for older runtimes and as the row set painted while the request is in flight or after it fails - so the list never blanks and a failed search is never an empty list. The answer is applied only when its echoed `query` equals the box's own value; the debounce plus that echo check is the whole cancellation mechanism, because an IPC `invoke` cannot be aborted. The no-match subline is per engine: 'update text is not searched' is true of the client matcher and false of the index, so the block renders the sentence belonging to whichever engine produced the rows on screen. NO NUMBER IN THIS NOTE IS A MEASUREMENT OF THE NEW PATH: latency, the first-keystroke frame stability and the index's own warm p95 are measured in the PR thread, not here.
